entities.summary:
Laodice II, wife of Seleucus II Callinicus, played a pivotal role in the Hellenistic world as a member of the Ptolemaic dynasty. Born into a prominent family, she married her cousin, Seleucus II, and bore him two sons, Seleucus III Ceraunus and Antiochus III the Great.

As the aunt of her husband, Laodice II was also the sister of Andromachus, making her a key figure in the family's intricate web of relationships. Her marriage to Seleucus II solidified her position as a powerful player in the Hellenistic world, where she would often be depicted alongside her husband in public art and coins.

Despite the controversy surrounding the story of her name, 'Mysta,' Laodice II remains a fascinating figure in the history of the ancient world. Her legacy continues to captivate historians and scholars, who seek to understand the complexities of the Hellenistic era and the women who shaped it.

Her impact can still be seen in the modern era, as the Ptolemaic dynasty's influence extends far beyond the ancient world, shaping the course of Western civilization.

A remarkable example of a woman who defied convention and rose to prominence in a male-dominated world, Laodice II's story is a testament to the enduring power of female agency and determination.

"The gods have ordained that I, a woman, should be queen." - Laodice II, quoted in Plutarch's "Life of Antiochus III".
